findings.title: Tests depend on live, mutable project documents
findings.description: The CLI and core tests read real files from `project-documents/user/slices/`: slices 212, 213, 214 and 928. Slice 214 is also the base text for the broken-copy fixtures. I confirmed all four files exist today. Real-format input is a project convention, so using the real template is reasonable. The slice documents are different. They are working artifacts, and anyone who edits, renames or archives one will break an unrelated validator test. The `brokenCopy()` regex `^## Value\n[\s\S]*?(?=^## Technical Scope$)` also depends on 214's exact section order. If that heading is reordered, the regex stops matching and the test fails with a misleading assertion. It would also break on CRLF. The same `withoutValueSection` helper is copied in both test files, which is a DRY violation. Prefer a small checked-in fixture design in `tests/fixtures/`, plus a single shared helper. Keep the real template as the real-world check.

findings.title: A frontmatter read error is silently reported as a docType failure
findings.description: `parseFrontmatter` wraps its whole body in `catch { return empty; }` (frontmatterParser.ts:63-65). `validateFile` calls it, then reads the same file again with `readFile`. If the first read fails after `preflight`, for example from a race or an I/O error, the file gets `reason: 'doctype'`. That misreports an unreadable file as a content problem and contradicts the module's "usage problems throw" contract. The explicit try/catch around the second `readFile` is therefore partly unreachable in practice. Reading the file once would fix both the error handling and the double I/O. You could read the text once, parse the frontmatter from the text, and keep the explicit error. That needs a text-based frontmatter parser, which the existing helper may not offer.

findings.title: Heading matching edge cases inherited from the bash port
findings.description:
- A required template heading whose text is only a placeholder, such as `## {name}`, normalizes to an empty key. `startsWith('')` then lets any same-level document heading satisfy it.
- `/<!--.*-->/g` is greedy, so a heading with two comments loses the text between them.
- Fence detection toggles on any line starting with three backticks. It ignores `~~~` fences, indented fences and longer fences that contain shorter ones.

These are probably acceptable for strict parity with the guide script. Consider a one-line comment saying the parity is deliberate, or a guard that rejects empty required keys.

findings.title: Error types are inconsistent with the rest of the CLI
findings.description: "No files given" throws core's `SliceDesignValidationError`. The other failures in the same file throw `UserError`. `handleError` treats the core error as a generic `Error`, so JSON output carries `code: 'UNKNOWN'` and human output gets an `Error:` prefix. The `UserError` instances also carry no `ErrorCode`. Mapping both to `UserError` with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` or `MISSING_CONFIG` would give consistent machine-readable output. The test file is `validate-design.test.ts` but the source is `validateDesign.ts`, which departs from the "mirror the source file name" convention. This is minor.

findings.title: Structure, typing and core design
findings.description: The pure validator and the file layer are cleanly separated, and the CLI is a thin wrapper. Preflight runs before any result is produced, so callers never see partial output next to an error. There is no `any`, exported functions have return types, and `as const` is used instead of an enum. Constants are defined once and reused. Test coverage of exit codes, JSON output, worktree resolution and ordering is thorough.
